title: Roast Chicken
subtitle: Classic British Sunday roast chicken with pan gravy
excerpt: A whole chicken roasted at high heat for crisp skin and juicy meat, with a simple pan gravy made from the drippings. The most reliable Sunday roast there is, and one of the best.

recipe.sourceNotes: Roasting a whole chicken is one of the fundamental techniques of British and European home cooking. The method is straightforward: season, roast at high heat for most of the time, rest thoroughly before carving. The drippings in the roasting tin make an immediate pan gravy. The French approach (poulet rôti) and the British approach are essentially the same dish with minor variations in aromatics. Resting the bird for at least 15 minutes after removing it from the oven is the step most often skipped and most consequential: a properly rested chicken loses far less juice when carved.

recipeTools.notes: For checking doneness at the thigh joint.

content.text: Take the chicken out of the fridge at least 30 minutes before it goes in the oven: a cold bird straight from the fridge cooks unevenly. Pat the skin dry with kitchen paper before seasoning: moisture is the enemy of crisp skin. Roast breast-side up the whole time. The chicken is done when the juices run clear when you pierce the thigh at its thickest point, or when a thermometer reads 75 C at the thigh joint (not touching bone). Rest for at least 15 minutes before carving.

items.preparation: 2 halved for the cavity, 2 minced for the butter
4 for the cavity, 2 chopped for the butter

content.text: Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Mix the softened butter with the minced garlic and chopped thyme. Pat the chicken dry. Rub the butter all over the skin, getting into any creases. Season generously with salt and pepper. Stuff the cavity with the halved lemon, halved garlic cloves, and thyme sprigs.

Place breast-side up in a roasting tin. Roast at 220 C for 20 minutes until the skin begins to colour. Reduce the heat to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. Roast for a further 50 to 60 minutes, basting twice, until the juices run clear at the thigh. Rest in a warm place for at least 15 minutes before carving.

Make the gravy: place the roasting tin over a medium heat. Add the flour to the drippings and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer, scraping up the browned bits. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until thickened. Season and strain into a jug. Carve the chicken and serve with the gravy.
